title: Comparing — more, most, and like
title_target: ঢাকা জাকার্তার চেয়ে ছোট — Dha-ka ja-kar-tar ché-yé chho-To
goal: Compare two things and name the best — with one surprise: Bengali has no word for “more”, and adjectives never change form.
bekal: saying “the same” with সমান and একই রকম
giving your opinion without giving offense

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — Comparing two cities
dialogs.intro: The last evening before Ani leaves for Sylhet. On the roof, Mitali and Rahim ask how Dhaka compares with Jakarta. Notice that the adjectives stay bare — there's no “more” anywhere.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Dhaka and Jakarta — which is bigger?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Jakarta is bigger than Dhaka. But the crowds are just the same.
lines.literal: Jakarta — Dhaka-of — than — big. but — crowd — same — kind.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Ha ha! And the heat? Where is it hotter?
lines.literal: ha ha! and — heat? where — more?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Jakarta is hot all year. Dhaka has a winter, which is nice.
lines.literal: Jakarta — whole — year — hot. Dhaka-in — winter — is-there, that — good.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Bengali food is like ours — rice, fish, spicy.
lines.literal: Bengali — food — our — food-of — like — rice, fish, spicy.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: So what did you like best?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Hilsa. The hardest fish in the world, but the tastiest!
lines.literal: hilsa. world-of — most — difficult — fish, but — most — tasty-of!

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Exactly! And what was the hardest thing about the language?
lines.literal: completely — right! and — most — difficult — what — was — language-in?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Half past three! Twice I showed up an hour early.
lines.literal: half-past — three-o'clock! I — two-times — one — hour — before — went.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Ha ha ha! Everyone gets that wrong, don't worry.
lines.literal: ha ha ha! that — everyone — mistake — does, worry — will-do — don't.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: But my Bengali is better than before, right?
lines.literal: but — my — Bengali — before-of — than — good — has-become, right — not?

notes: ⚠️ **Bengali has no word for “more”, and adjectives don't change form.** To say “Jakarta is bigger than Dhaka”, the pattern is **জাকার্তা ঢাকার চেয়ে বড়** — literally “Jakarta, Dhaka-than, big”. **বড়** stays বড়; there's no form like *bigger* or *more big*. The word **চেয়ে** does all the comparing.

**The thing compared takes the possessive ending -র · -এর, then চেয়ে.** ঢাকা**র** চেয়ে (than Dhaka), আমা**র** চেয়ে (than me), আগে**র** চেয়ে (than before). ⚠️ The ending is required; *ঢাকা চেয়ে* sounds wrong at once. Another form with the same meaning is **-এর থেকে**, and the two are interchangeable.

**For “most”, use সবচেয়ে — literally “than all”.** সবচেয়ে বড় (biggest), সবচেয়ে ভালো (best), সবচেয়ে কঠিন (hardest). ⚠️ It's the same word — চেয়ে — with সব (all) in front. Once you see that, the whole group is one rule, not two.

**The word বেশি (more) can be added, but often isn't needed.** ঢাকার চেয়ে **বেশি** গরম (hotter than Dhaka) is fine, but ঢাকার চেয়ে গরম is enough. ⚠️ English speakers tend to always add “more”, and it sounds wordy. Get used to dropping বেশি unless you really want to stress the amount.

**“Like” is formed with … -এর মতো.** আমাদের খাবারের মতো (like our food), আপনার মতো (like you), সমুদ্রের মতো (like the sea). ⚠️ মতো always comes **after** the thing compared and needs the possessive ending — the same pattern as সামনে and কাছে in Unit 7.

**For “the same”, there are two words with different feels.** **একই রকম** *èk-i rô-kôm* means “alike, much the same” and is used for casual comparisons. **সমান** *sôman* means “exactly equal in size or amount” and is more precise: দুটো ঘর সমান (the two rooms are the same size).

**Giving opinions gently is a skill more useful than vocabulary.** Compare **এটা ভালো না** (this isn't good) with **আমার ঠিক ভালো লাগেনি** (it wasn't quite for me). ⚠️ The second is far safer, especially about food, religion, and politics — three topics you'll often be asked about. A lifesaver: **আমি ঠিক জানি না** (I'm not really sure).

grammars.title: More, most, like
after: **কোনটা?** *konTa* means “which one?” and always shows up in comparison questions: কোনটা বড়? (which is bigger?), কোনটা ভালো? (which is better?). For people, use **কে**: কে লম্বা? (who is taller?).

grammars.title: Adjectives for comparing
after: ⚠️ **হালকা means light — not just in weight, but also in taste, color, and work.** হালকা খাবার (light food), হালকা রং (pale color), হালকা কাজ (light work). You'll hear it often at the table after you've been ill.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Three questions you'll be asked a lot
items: **“Which is better, our country or yours?”** The best answer isn't to choose, but to name what's different: **দুটোই সুন্দর, কিন্তু আলাদা** (both are beautiful, but different). Over-the-top praise just sounds insincere.
**“Is our food too spicy for you?”** A pleasing answer: **আমাদের খাবারও ঝাল!** (our food is spicy too!). Similarities always charm more than differences — use one if it's true for you.

**“Do you like Bangladesh / West Bengal?”** Name one **specific** thing — the people, the rivers, morning tea, a song you heard on a rooftop. A general “it's nice” will be politely accepted, but a specific answer will be remembered.

blocks.text: A note on arguing. Bengalis have a reputation — one they're proud of — for loving long discussions about anything: literature, politics, football, and which fish is tastiest. A conversation that sounds like a quarrel is often just an **আড্ডা** in full swing. ⚠️ You don't have to pick a side; **আমি ঠিক জানি না, আপনারা বলুন** (I'm not really sure, you tell me) will be welcomed, and you'll still count as part of the circle.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the possessive ending + চেয়ে.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: সবচেয়ে বড় — সবচেয়ে ভালো — সবচেয়ে কঠিন — সবচেয়ে সস্তা
জাকার্তা ঢাকার চেয়ে বড়। — ইলিশ সবচেয়ে ভালো মাছ। — বাংলা খাবার আমাদের খাবারের মতো। — ভিড় একই রকম। — আপনার কী মনে হয়?
ঢাকা জাকার্তার চেয়ে ছোট। — এটা সবচেয়ে ভালো। — সে আমার চেয়ে লম্বা। — খাবারটা আমাদের খাবারের মতো। — দুটোই ভালো। — আপনার কী মনে হয়?
